subject: PillarCare — post-demo follow-up: data use, residency, and audit request
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jason Brooks <jason.brooks@pillarcare.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PillarCare — post-demo follow-up: data use, residency, and audit request

Hi Jason — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we’re aligned on next steps: 

1) Data-use commitment (PillarCare request)
   - You asked that any customer content processed by Redwood not be used to improve shared model weights, retrain models, or inform system-wide model updates. In short: no learning-on-customer-data and no weight updates from your traffic.

2) Logging & retention
   - You requested minimal logging of PII and a 30‑day retention window for request/response logs unless a longer retention is required for debugging a specific incident (with prior notice).

3) Residency and encryption
   - Primary requirement: EU residency for both inference and audit logs. All stored logs should be encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) where available.

4) Audit & evidence
   - You asked for regular evidence that training data is not derived from your traffic (audit trail), and a copy of Redwood's SOC 2 report and data-handling addendum for legal review.

Next steps (action items):
- Rachel: I will share an initial Redwood Data Addendum (attached) and a short summary of the runtime controls that enforce the no-learning commitment.
- Jason: Please confirm in writing that the above matches PillarCare’s expectations and attach any additional legal wording you need.
- Sean/Laura: If legal agrees, please prepare a contract addendum with the residency and retention clauses (cc’d).

Attachment: redwood-data-addendum_v1.pdf (pdf) — draft addendum that includes no-learning clause, residency, log retention, and KMS options.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the legal draft and the SOC 2 link.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Jason Brooks <jason.brooks@pillarcare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: PillarCare Legal <legal@pillarcare.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PillarCare — post-demo follow-up: data use, residency, and audit request

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our understanding. A few clarifications from PillarCare: 

- Explicit wording: We need an explicit contract clause that states "Redwood will not use PillarCare customer traffic to update, retrain, or improve model weights made available to other customers." That must be auditable.
- Logs: We accept a 30-day rolling retention for standard logs but require that any logs flagged for debugging are deleted within 7 days after the incident is resolved unless we authorize otherwise.
- Residency: EU residency is mandatory for inference and logs — specifically, data must be processed and stored within EU-based cloud regions (no cross-border backups).
- Evidence: Please provide a SOC 2 Type II report and a short operational note describing the technical enforcement for the no-learning guarantee (e.g., configuration flags, disabled telemetry paths, and KV cache policies).

I’ve attached PillarCare's privacy requirements doc for legal to reference. We can mark up the addendum once Redwood sends a draft suitable for signature.

Attachment: PillarCare_privacy_requirements.docx (docx)

—Jason
Jason Brooks
Head of Security & Privacy, PillarCare
jason.brooks@pillarcare.com

- Ops: Rachel, capture the technical enforcement plan from Platform — we need an ops note that explains how "no-learning" is enforced (flags, disabled telemetry, and isolation of customer KV caches). Put the ops note in Drive and link in the addendum.
